parts.note: front of house is theatre talk for the area facing the audience, so the alarm is the nerves an actor feels facing them

explanation.surface: A fire alarm or burglar alarm fitted at the front of a home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Front of house' sounds like the street side of a home, but in theatres it means the audience side of the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervous panic before performing to an audience is what actors call this condition.

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Sumerian city

explanation.surface: A trip to see an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: A journey visiting several places is a trip or expedition.

definitions.meaning: to rook is to swindle or cheat
a common grey and white bird of the coast

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to dupe or cheat someone; the noun is a common coastal bird.

clue.text: Plant agent on the fourth of July

parts.note: a factor is an agent who acts for another

indicators.note: the fourth of points at the fourth letter of the word July

explanation.surface: Planting a spy on Independence Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The fourth of July' looks like the US holiday, but means the fourth letter of JULY, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An industrial plant is a building where goods are manufactured.

clue.text: Terrible fellow and vain, in a way

indicators.note: in a way suggests the letters of vain arranged after a fashion

explanation.surface: A dreadful man who is also conceited.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivan the Terrible was the first tsar of Russia; 'in a way' rearranges VAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The first Russian tsar was known by the nickname 'the Terrible'.

clue.text: Ribbon Tam O'Shanter disallowed, you say?

indicators.note: you say points to spoken words that sound like the entry

parts.note: a Tam O'Shanter is a Scottish cap, so this is a hat banned

explanation.surface: A ribbon on a Scottish cap that has been prohibited.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tam O'Shanter is a Scottish woollen bonnet, so 'Tam O'Shanter disallowed' is HAT BANNED, spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of cloth or ribbon around a hat's crown above the brim.

clue.text: Hypersensitive to criticism yet with not much to hide?

definitions.meaning: easily hurt or offended by criticism
hide is skin, so having only a slight covering of skin

explanation.definitionFit: Over-sensitive people are said to have little protective skin, and hide is another word for skin.

parts.note: porter is a dark beer
a public house is a tavern

explanation.surface: Steak and a pint at a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A prime beef cut from the thick end of the short loin.

parts.note: driving off here means chasing away an unwanted animal or person, not leaving in a car or hitting a golf ball

explanation.surface: The sound of a car engine starting as someone pulls away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driving off' suggests motoring or golf; it means sending a cat or bird away with a cry.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the exclamation used to scare away a pest or intruder.

clue.text: Moulded plastic tube is the people's choice

indicators.note: plastic that is moulded is pressed into a new shape, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A moulded plastic tube is the product consumers prefer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moulded' reshapes PLASTIC TUBE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: What appeals to ordinary members of the public is popular preference or general liking.

clue.text: Loop equipment round head of needle

indicators.note: the kit goes round, enclosing the other letter

parts.note: a kit is a set of equipment

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Wrap gear around the tip of a sewing needle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts N, the first letter of 'needle', inside KIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To make stitches by looping yarn with needles is to make woollen fabric this way.

clue.text: Tipsy, I starch foolishly and get such shrinking!

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Tipsy, I starch foolishly and get such shrinking!': the anagram fodder TIPSY I STARCH has ST to spare and lacks a C for PSYCHIATRIC (3 letters off); printed text not found by search
annotationWithheld.clue: Tipsy, I starch foolishly and get such shrinking!

clue.text: Conjuring to be light tomorrow, in France

parts.note: leger is French for light
demain is French for tomorrow

explanation.surface: A magic trick is meant to be lightweight tomorrow in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in France' tells you to put both words into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight of hand used in magic tricks.

clue.text: Wrong set-drawback for waiter on board

indicators.note: something wrong is amiss or out of order, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: read as draw back: the word draw written back to front

explanation.surface: A setback that was a mistaken draw in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' jumbles SET to STE; 'drawback' is read as DRAW back, giving WARD. The hyphen in 'set-drawback' hides the split.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship or plane, an attendant who serves passengers food and drink holds this job title.

clue.text: Bardic tales include some popular sayings

indicators.note: include some says the words contain a portion of the entry

explanation.surface: A bard's tales contain several well-known sayings.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of a Latin word for a pronouncement or maxim.

parts.note: read not as the Hertfordshire town but as the table where someone pots balls

explanation.surface: Potters Bar, a commuter town just north of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Potters Bar is a town in Hertfordshire; here a potter pots balls, and a bar is a game played on a table.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue game on a green baize table where players pot coloured balls in turn.

indicators.note: rotten fruit goes bad and the word plums is broken up

explanation.surface: Rotten plums drop from the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A decline or sudden drop is a downturn.

indicators.note: first means take the opening letter of the word You
about signals the letters of lied moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: You were the first to lie about the harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: Y, the first letter of 'You', then 'about' rearranges LIED to IELD.
explanation.definitionFit: A crop's output, the amount a field produces, is its return.

clue.text: Reported lines of people waiting for reminders

indicators.note: reported signals a word spoken rather than spelt, matching its sound

parts.note: lines of waiting people are queues

explanation.surface: Lines of people were reportedly waiting to be reminded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reported' gives the sound of QUEUES, spelt as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompts given to actors to remind them when to speak are signals of this kind.

clue.text: Loosen up a party in Paris?

parts.note: in French the article a is un
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Relax at a party in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Paris' tells you to put 'a' into French: UN. DO is a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten or untie something is to slacken it.

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the word Times could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Pieces published in the Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges TIMES. The Times is a British newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Separate objects or things in a list are articles.

definitions.meaning: written in lines of metre, as two words
turned the other way round, reversed in order

explanation.definitionFit: Split as two words it means written in metre; as one word it means opposite or reversed.

clue.text: Some beginning to be open-handed? How unoriginal!

indicators.note: beginning takes the opening letter of the word Some

parts.note: lavish means generous or open-handed

explanation.surface: Some people start being generous, but it is copycat behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: S, the first letter of 'Some', then LAVISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Copying something closely and without originality, like a servant.

clue.text: End of booked passage finds article in a state

indicators.note: in places the article inside the other piece

parts.note: the book A Passage to India ends with the word India
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Finishing a booked journey, a newspaper piece reports on a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Booked passage' is E. M. Forster's novel A Passage to India, whose title ends in INDIA; 'in' places AN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Midwestern US state whose capital is Indianapolis.

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
pairs of sweethearts are lovers

explanation.surface: Quiet pairs of a type of wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapwings are birds of the family of wading birds also called peewits.

definitions.meaning: a great volume is a large heavy book
towards me, written as two words

explanation.definitionFit: A large book is a weighty volume; split in two the word means towards the speaker.

indicators.note: headless means the opening letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: the Oscar is the film-award statuette

explanation.surface: The trademark of a statuette that has lost its head.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand is a mark burned into skin, which leaves this kind of mark.

definitions.meaning: firmly fixed, as in sound asleep

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to abstain from eating; the adjective means firm or secure, as in a deep sleep.

indicators.note: tailless means the closing letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: an aircraft is a plane

explanation.surface: Design drawings of an aircraft with no tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A blueprint is a detailed design or scheme.

definitions.meaning: done sensibly and realistically, with a focus on usefulness

explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means both sensibly and realistically, and nearly or virtually.

parts.note: bis is Latin and musical notation for twice or repeat

explanation.surface: Say I twice and you receive the bird, a boo from an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: BIS means twice, used on scores and in French for an encore.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-billed wading bird sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Solid foundation for cricket at home?

definitions.text: Solid foundation for cricket at home?

parts.words: Solid foundation for cricket at home?
parts.note: the cricket is the chirping insect of Dickens's Cricket on the Hearth, and its home base is the stone floor before the fire

explanation.surface: A firm base for playing cricket in your own grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket suggests the sport; it is the insect, which traditionally lives by the fireside.
explanation.definitionFit: The flat stone forming the floor of a fireplace is a solid foundation in the home.
